title: He didn’t wait for permission.
paragraphs: And at first… it looked like it worked.
Dust hung in the air over Shechem. Voices whispered. Deals were made in corners. Silver exchanged hands. Loyalty was bought—not earned.
Abimelech, the son no one expected, stood at the center of it all.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
You can take a throne without ever receiving authority.
And that difference will eventually cost you everything.
He gathered support the way many still do today—through influence, manipulation, and proximity to power. He spoke what people wanted to hear. He positioned himself as the answer.
And then came the moment that revealed everything.
A single survivor left to tell the story.
And maybe you’ve never gone that far…
But if you’re honest, you’ve felt it.
To force doors open instead of waiting for Him to open them.
To be seen, even if it means stepping outside His will.
If this found you, it’s not by accident.
Because the spirit behind Abimelech’s rise is still alive today.
From the outside, it looked stable. Successful, even.
Because God never endorsed what flesh tries to manufacture.
The very people Abimelech used to rise… turned against him.
And the man who crowned himself…
This is the breaking point most ignore:
Sin doesn’t just destroy others—it builds your own downfall.
But if God didn’t call it…
And that’s where the story stops being about Abimelech…
Because the real issue isn’t just ambition.
The desire to replace God’s authority with your own.
To rule your life without surrender.
To sit on a throne your soul was never meant to carry.
But here’s the part many miss…
God didn’t leave us in that condition.
Originally written by Gospel Warrior, this truth cuts deep:
Where self-exaltation brings death… Christ brings life through surrender.
And through His death and resurrection, He offers something Abimelech could never secure:
A kingdom that cannot be shaken.
You don’t fix this by trying harder.
You don’t earn your way back.
And you trust in Jesus Christ alone—His grace, His finished work on the cross.
But here’s what most people don’t realize…
You’re either building something God is blessing…
Or something He will eventually break.
If something in you feels exposed right now… that’s not condemnation.
New teachings are added almost daily.
Am I called… or just climbing?
Because one path ends in collapse.
The other leads to the cross…
